info.title: openGym API
info.summary: Passkey (WebAuthn) auth + per-user state storage for openGym
info.description:
The backend of [openGym](https://opengym.ch), a free, open-source
gym & body-weight tracker. A Bun server routed by Hono, JSON-file storage,
HMAC-signed session cookies. This document is generated from the route definitions in
`api/openapi/` and served at `/api/openapi.json`; `/api/docs` browses it.

### Authentication
Sign-in is by **passkey** (WebAuthn, via `@simplewebauthn/server`). A successful
`register/verify` or `login/verify` sets the session cookie; every authenticated
route then works with that cookie. The paired mobile app has no shared cookie jar,
so it redeems a short pairing code (`/api/pair/redeem`) for the *same* signed token
and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead.

An instance started with `PASSWORD_LOGIN=1` also offers **name-and-password
sign-in** (tag `password`): opt-in per profile, scrypt-hashed, throttled, with an
admin-issued one-time reset code instead of e-mail. A profile may also add an e-mail
address to sign in with instead of its name (`/api/account/email`); no mail is ever
sent to it. Its routes set exactly the same cookie. With the flag off (the default)
every one of them answers 404.

### Throttling
The `password` routes are counted per client address: at most 60 requests a minute
across them, and wrong answers (a password, a reset code, an invite code on password
signup, an e-mail address already in use) pause the address from the 21st on, for 30 s,
doubling up to 15 min. Wrong passwords also pause the *account* they were tried
against from the 6th on, for 1 min doubling up to 1 h (the same pause whether the account
was named by its name or its e-mail), and an identifier that names no account is
paused the same way, as typed. A password check counts from the moment it
starts, so checks sent at once get no more tries than checks sent one by one. A
paused caller gets `429 {"error": …, "code": "locked", "retryAfter": <s>}` with a
`Retry-After` header. Passkey sign-up and sign-in and the pairing routes are not
throttled (their failures reach the audit log at most ten a minute per address).
The two routes that redeem a one-time device link (tag `passkeys`) share
the per-address budget, and wrong codes pause the address for link redemption only,
from the 21st on, the way wrong reset codes do. Adding or removing a passkey in Settings
(`POST /api/account/passkeys/options`, `DELETE /api/account/passkeys`) and making a
device code (`POST /api/account/device-link`) spend the per-address budget too, and a
current password given there as proof counts like one given at sign-in.
The address is the socket's, or with `TRUST_PROXY=1` the one a trusted proxy put in
`CF-Connecting-IP` / the last `X-Forwarded-For` entry / `X-Real-IP`; IPv6 clients are
counted by /64. Counters live in memory and reset on restart.

### Sessions
The cookie/bearer value is `<payload>.<hmac>` where the payload is
`<uid>:<expiry-ms>:<session-version>`, signed with a per-instance secret
(HMAC-SHA256). Sessions last `SESSION_DAYS` (default 90). `POST /api/logout/all`
bumps the user's session version, which invalidates every token ever issued for
the account.

### CSRF
State-changing browser requests must come from the app's own origin. The server
checks `Sec-Fetch-Site` (falling back to `Origin` vs the configured `ORIGIN`);
a mismatch is refused with `403 {"error":"cross-origin request refused","code":"origin-mismatch","expected":ORIGIN}` on any
non-GET route, the passkey routes included. Exempt: `pair/redeem`, which the mobile
app calls from its own origin (the code in the body is the credential, and the token
comes back in the body, never as a cookie), and any request a Bearer token
authenticates by itself: a valid session token, with no session cookie beside it, on
any route but the sign-in ones — the four passkey routes, the password and reset-code
routes and the two device-link routes, which act on the credential in the body, never
on a Bearer. A cross-origin request whose Bearer does not buy the exemption is refused
before any handler runs: `401 {"error":"not signed in"}` when that Bearer does not
verify and is the only credential (a paired app whose token was revoked or expired),
the 403 otherwise.
The passkey routes were exempt before, on the grounds that the challenge id is a
credential; but it is bound to nothing else, so a hostile page could complete the
attacker's own passkey sign-in in the victim's browser (login CSRF) and the answer
set the victim's session to the attacker's account. The password routes are **not**
exempt for the same reason: a hostile page knows a valid name and password of its own.

### Environment-dependent behavior
- `INVITE_ONLY=1`: registration requires a valid invite code (minted by an admin).
- `ALLOW_GUEST=0`: hides the client-side "continue without account" mode; the
  server merely reports the flag via `GET /api/config` (guest mode never talks to
  this API at all).
- `ADMIN_UIDS=<uid>,<uid>`: user ids treated as admins (a `"admin": true` flag on
  the user record in `db.json` works too). Admins get the `/api/admin/*` routes.
  One admin is the owner: the record with `"owner": true`, else the first
  `ADMIN_UIDS` entry with a profile, else the oldest admin. Only the owner appoints
  and removes admins, deletes an admin, hands the role on and clears the audit log.
- `FIRST_USER_ADMIN` (default off; `1` turns it on): the first profile registered
  on an instance with no profiles gets that `"admin": true` flag and is the owner. Decided at
  registration only, never applied to an instance that already has profiles.
- `AUDIT_LOG` (default on), `AUDIT_MAX` (default 5000 events), `AUDIT_DAYS`
  (default 90), `AUDIT_IP` (`off` | `net` | `full`, default off) shape the audit
  log served by `GET /api/admin/audit`.
- `PASSWORD_LOGIN=1`: adds the `password` routes and `password_login: true` in
  `GET /api/config`. Off by default.
- `OIDC_ISSUER` + `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` (and usually `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`): adds the `oidc`
  routes and `oidc` in `GET /api/config`. `OIDC_ONLY=1` refuses passkey and password
  sign-ups, and passkey and password sign-ins for everyone but admins (`403 oidc-only`).
- `DEFAULT_LANG` (e.g. `pt-BR`; unset by default): `default_lang` in `GET /api/config`,
  the language of the sign-in screen and of every profile that never picked one.
- `TRUST_PROXY=1`: the throttle reads the client address from proxy headers (set by
  the bundled `docker-compose.yml`, where only the web container can reach the API).
- `INTEGRATIONS` (unset by default, e.g. `webhook`): the providers of the `integrations`
  routes, and the `integrations` block of `GET /api/config`. `INTEGRATIONS_ALLOW_LAN=1`
  lets a webhook reach the home network (http too), never loopback or link-local.
- `MEDIA_UPLOADS` (default on; `0` removes the `media` routes and the `media` block of
  `GET /api/config`), `MEDIA_QUOTA_MB` (200 per profile, `0` = no cap),
  `MEDIA_IMAGE_MAX_MB` (2), `MEDIA_GIF_MAX_MB` (8), `MEDIA_VIDEO_MAX_MB` (100),
  `MEDIA_VIDEO_MAX_SEC` (60), `MEDIA_AUDIO_MAX_MB` (2), `MEDIA_GC_GRACE_DAYS` (14), `MEDIA_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR` (600
  per profile), `MEDIA_MIN_FREE_MB` (512, `0` = no floor): photos and videos of custom
  exercises (tag `media`). Every MB here is 2^20 bytes.

### Conventions
- Every response body is JSON with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The one exception is
  `GET /api/media/{hash}`, which answers with the stored file itself
  (`Cache-Control: private, no-store`).
- Errors are always `{"error": "<human-readable message>"}`. The `password`, throttle and
  `media` routes add a stable `code` for the client to word in its own language.
- Unknown method+path pairs return `404 {"error":"not found"}`; an unhandled
  exception returns `500 {"error":"server error"}`.
- Every route that reads a request body requires `Content-Type: application/json`
  (a `charset` parameter is fine) and answers any other type with
  `415 {"error":"content-type must be application/json"}` — the types a form can
  send are the ones that skip the CORS preflight, which is how a cross-site form
  reached these routes. A request with no body needs no Content-Type. A body that does
  not parse, or parses to anything but an object (`null`, a string, an array), is
  `400 {"error":"invalid json"}` on every route that reads one; an empty body counts
  as `{}`. A body over 5 MiB is `413 {"error":"body too large"}`; the rest of the
  upload is discarded so the answer reaches the client.
- CORS: the request's `Origin` is reflected in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`
  **without** `Allow-Credentials`, so cross-origin callers can only ever
  authenticate with a Bearer token, never with the cookie.

servers.description: Same origin as the openGym web app (the normal deployment)

tags.name: pairing
tags.description: Mobile-app pairing (code from a signed-in browser tab)

tags.name: oidc
tags.description: Sign in with an identity provider (OpenID Connect), next to passkeys. Every route here is a 404 unless the server runs with `OIDC_ISSUER` and `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` (docs/SELF_HOSTING.md, "Sign in with your identity provider").

tags.name: password
tags.description: Optional name-and-password sign-in (`PASSWORD_LOGIN=1`). Every route here is a 404 while the flag is off.

tags.name: passkeys
tags.description: More than one passkey on a profile: list, add, rename, remove, plus one-time device links, which let another device of the same person add a passkey of its own.

tags.name: data
tags.description: Per-user state sync (the whole app state as one JSON blob)

tags.name: push
tags.description: Web Push (VAPID) subscriptions, rest-timer and test pushes

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Admin dashboard. Requires an admin session (`ADMIN_UIDS` or `admin:true`)

tags.name: media
tags.description: The photo, GIF or video of a user's own custom exercise, and the photos and videos attached to a logged workout. Stored per profile (one quota for both) and named by the SHA-256 of its bytes; the state only carries a `MediaRef`. Every route here is a 404 when the instance runs with `MEDIA_UPLOADS=0`.

tags.name: coach
tags.description: AI Coach: plans, reviews and debriefs. Every route here answers 503 unless the instance has the Coach switched on and a provider connected.

tags.name: mcp
tags.description: The MCP connector's OAuth sign-in (docs/MCP_REMOTE.md), for Claude, ChatGPT and other assistants that add openGym by URL. Only with `MCP=on`, otherwise 404. What it issues is an ordinary scoped API token, made when the person approves it on the consent screen.

tags.name: trainers
tags.description: Trainers, gym leads and studios (docs/TRAINERS.md). Off unless the server runs with `TRAINERS=on`; then every route here answers, otherwise 404 `trainers-off`. A member connects to a trainer with the trainer's code and a consent, decides per category what is shared, and can change or end it any time, effective on the next request. Every route spends a per-account budget (429 `rate-limited`, Retry-After).

tags.name: shared
tags.description: The community library (`LIBRARY=on`, off by default): things people chose to share with everyone on this server, each after its own consent, always shown with who shared it and when. Importing copies the item into your own profile. Reports, admin review (`SHARE_REVIEW=on`), removal and bans are all logged. The built-in exercise media can never be shared (blocked by SHA-256). Every route spends a per-account budget.

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: Scoped tokens (docs/API_TOKENS.md): a key a profile makes in Settings for one program, an AI client over MCP, a planner, a script, holding per category `off`, `view` or `apply`. Only its SHA-256 is stored. A token reaches the `/api/token/*` routes and nothing else, never more than its profile, and ends with "sign out everywhere". `API_TOKENS=off` makes every route here a 404.

tags.name: integrations
tags.description: Settings → Integrations: outbound webhooks now, more providers later. Off unless the server runs with `INTEGRATIONS` (e.g. `INTEGRATIONS=webhook`); then a profile can add its own connections. Secrets are sealed at rest and shown once. See docs/INTEGRATIONS.md.

cookieAuth.name: gymsid
cookieAuth.description:
HMAC-signed session cookie, set by `register/verify` / `login/verify`.
On HTTPS deployments it is issued as **`__Host-gymsid`** (host-locked,
Secure); the unprefixed `gymsid` is what a plain-http `localhost` instance
uses, and is still accepted for pre-upgrade sessions. HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax;
browser clients never handle the value directly.

bearerAuth.description: The same signed session token, carried as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by the paired mobile app (obtained from `POST /api/pair/redeem`). Bearer requests skip the CSRF origin check; a browser never attaches this header on its own.

tokenAuth.description: A scoped token (`ogt_…`, Settings → API tokens), as `Authorization: Bearer ogt_…`. Only the `/api/token/*` routes accept it.

disabledByEnv.description: COACH_DISABLED is set, so nothing the admin toggles matters.

runtime.description: The runtime it spawns, when it spawns one.

connected.description: Whether a credential is already filed for it.

providers.description: Every provider this build knows, and what each one needs.

model.description: The model in force for the active provider.

models.description: Model per provider. Switching provider keeps them all.

knownModels.description: From the live check, when the provider could be asked.

maxMessageLen.description: How long a chat message, refinement or review note can be (200–4000, default 1000).

runtime.description: The live check performed while answering this request.

boundUid.description: The profile an instance credential bound itself to, once one has spent it.

auth.description: Whether a credential is filed, and whose. `unreadable` is its own state because it has a specific cause and a specific fix: ./data restored without its `secret`.

unprivileged.description: Whether the privilege drop can be performed. It fails closed: if `ok` is false no job runs at all, and the admin needs to hear that here rather than from a user.

lastError.description: The last failure the instance log recorded, or null.

recent.description: The last 20 jobs, newest first. Counts and outcomes only, never contents.

AdminCoach.description: The whole admin card in one answer. Never a credential, only whether one is filed.

owner.description: The one admin who manages the others.

email.description: PASSWORD_LOGIN instances only. The sign-in e-mail, if any.

resetUntil.description: PASSWORD_LOGIN instances only. Expiry (ms) of an unused reset code.

recoveryUntil.description: Expiry (ms) of an unused recovery code (POST /api/admin/user/recovery, recover.js).

data_view.description: true only with ADMIN_DATA_VIEW on: then routines, bodyweight and workouts are present.

bytes.description: Size of the state file on disk.

roles.description: TRAINERS on only. Studio roles, free-trainer status, gyms joined.

grants.description: TRAINERS on only. Active sharing grants of this member.

w.description: The day's weight in `unit` (see the description).

t.description: When the day was last edited (ms)

src.description: Set when every weigh-in of the day was read from a health app or a file.

id.description: Unique within the day. '0' is the weigh-in a day from before held.

at.description: Local time of day, HH:MM; null when not known.

t.description: When this weigh-in was last edited (ms).

src.description: Read from a health app or a file.

sid.description: The health app's own id of the sample.

gone.description: Weigh-ins removed from a day that keeps others, id → when (ms).

BodyweightEntry.description: One day of weigh-ins. `w` is the day's one value, the one the profile's `bwDaily` setting picks from `ins` (first, the default; avg; last), so a reader that knows nothing of `ins` gets the same number the app charts. A day from before v1.4.4 has no `ins`: one weigh-in without a time. A client that writes `w` and `t` of a day with `ins` (an older app correcting the day) has that taken as a correction of the weigh-in `w` came from.

prs.description: Exercise ids that hit a personal record.

media.description: Photos and videos attached to this workout (a progress photo, a form-check clip), at most six in the app. Refs only; the bytes are behind `/api/media/{hash}`, and the server keeps every file any entry here names (the GC walks this list as it walks each custom exercise's `media`).

_ts.description: When this workout was last edited after it was logged, ms, for merging two devices' copies.

kind.description: `gif` means animated; a one-frame GIF is an `image`. `audio` is a sound of the user's own (`sounds`); its width and height are 1.

dur.description: Seconds, one decimal; videos and animated GIFs, absent when unknown.

poster.description: A still of at most 480 px, always for images and GIFs, when possible for videos.

MediaRef.description: What the state knows of an uploaded file. The bytes are behind `GET /api/media/{hash}`; the server keeps a file as long as some `customEx[].media.hash`, `workouts[].media[].hash` or `.poster.hash` of either in the profile's state names it, and for `MEDIA_GC_GRACE_DAYS` after.

owner.description: The one admin who manages the others.

invitedBy.description: The invite code this account was created with.

lastWorkout.description: ISO day of the newest workout.

hasPush.description: Has at least one push subscription.

password.description: PASSWORD_LOGIN instances only. The profile has a password.

email.description: PASSWORD_LOGIN instances only. The e-mail the profile signs in with, if any.

kind.description: Set on a calendar feed's token

connector.description: Made by an assistant's connector sign-in: which assistant, and the client name it registered.

TokenScopes.description: Per category `off`, `view` or `apply` (notes at most `view`). Missing is `off`.

id.description: Monotonic, never reset; a cleared log leaves a visible id gap.

msg.description: Short detail: a failure reason code, or the invite code involved. Rejected invite guesses and unknown credential ids are deliberately never recorded.

ip.description: Only when AUDIT_IP is on: the full address (`full`) or just the network, /24 or /48 (`net`).

AuditEvent.description: One line of the audit log.

done.description: Finished workouts are in it too.

CoachCap.description: What this profile has spent of its daily allowance.

minPeople.description: Three. Below it nothing is computed at all.

unit.description: The reader's own unit. Every number below is in it.

rankPct.description: Share of the others at or below this profile, averaged over the listed exercises.

CoachCohort.description:
Medians across the profiles that opted in, and where this one stands among them.
`ok` is false whenever there is nothing to show, and the other flags say why:
the admin has the comparison switched off (`enabled: false`), this profile does
not share (`sharing: false`), or there are not yet three who do.

limitations.description: Injuries and anything to work around.

CoachIntake.description: The intake answers, as the plan screen collects them. Stored in the profile's own state as well; sent here so a plan can be asked for with answers that have not been synced yet.

planHash.description: The plan this was written against. A later edit makes it stale.

trigger.description: Present when an automatic review made it, which nobody was watching for.

before.description: What the plan says now. The client checks it before applying.

changes.description: A review's change-set, each one applied or rejected on its own.

bundle.description: A whole plan, from a `create` job (routines, week and any custom exercises).

score.description: A debrief's score for the session.

CoachProposal.description:
The answer waiting for a decision, from whichever kind of job produced it. It
expires 14 days after it was made; the first status poll after that retires it.
`changes` comes from a review, `bundle` from a plan, `score`/`highlights` from a
debrief. One of the three, never more.

job.description: The job running now, or null. One at a time per profile.

maxMessageLen.description:
The longest note or refinement this instance keeps, in characters. It rides on the
poll so a chat that is already open follows an admin's change.

errorClass.description:
Why a failed job failed. Provider failures are sorted by cause:
`auth` (the credential was refused), `quota` (out of quota or rate limited),
`schema` (the endpoint will not serve the request shape), `outage` (5xx past
the retries), `unreachable` (nothing answered), `timeout` (no answer in the
job budget), `missing` (no key or runtime), `provider` (anything else it
refused), `unusable` (it answered outside the contract). Job-level classes:
`restart`, `forgotten`, `consent`, `noworkout`, `toolarge`, `nostate`, `off`.

message.description:
The short user-facing line for that failure, when the class has one. Present
only on failures a provider caused; a client that has its own translated
line for `errorClass` may prefer it. Never contains provider detail.

trigger.description: Present when it was an automatic review.

reading.description: Present on `nochange`: why there was nothing to change.

last.description: How the most recent job ended, so the chat can say so in the Coach's own voice.

url.description: One link: a video or a guide. http(s) only, no credentials. Neither the app nor the server ever fetches it: the app opens it in a new browsing context on a tap.

_ts.description: When this entry was last edited, ms, for merging two devices' copies.

CustomExercise.description: One exercise the user made (representative shape). The server stores it as sent and reads only `media` from it, to know which uploaded files are still referenced.

error.description: Human-readable message. This is the only error shape the API has.

code.description: A stable reason on the password, throttle and media routes, for a client to word in its own language (`bad-credentials`, `locked`, `too-short`, `media-quota`, …). Media refusals add the numbers to word it with (`maxMB`, `maxSec`, `usedMB`, `quotaMB`).

retryAfter.description: 429 only. The same number of seconds as the Retry-After header.

expected.description: A refused cross-origin request (`origin-mismatch`): the ORIGIN this server expects.

issues.description: A request whose shape the spec does not allow (`invalid-request`): what is wrong, at most 20.

missing.description: Files a shared item names that are not uploaded yet (409).

consent.description: The consent text to agree to first (409 `consent`).

rev.description: The current version of a shared item (412).

status.description: An inbox item that is no longer open (410 `not-open`): what it is now.

lastOk.description: Epoch ms of the last delivery that landed.

failures.description: Failed attempts since the last success.

failed.description: Deliveries given up on; Retry sends them again.

IntegrationEvent.description: `workout.finished`: a workout reached the server (from any device). `workout.pr`: that workout set personal records. `weighin.logged`: a new or changed weigh-in. Only events from the last seven days that happened after the connection was made are sent.

usedBy.description: User id that redeemed the code (absent/null while unused).

active.description: The session as the app holds it (`entries` and the rest), or null.

unit.description: The unit the session's numbers are in.

at.description: The writer's stamp (milliseconds); the newest wins.

builtin.description: This instance keeps a photo or video of your own on a built-in exercise too (`exMedia`). Absent on an instance from before.

imageMB.description: A photo after the app re-encoded it, or a poster.

audioMB.description: A sound of the user's own (a WAV of at most 30 s).

sounds.description: This instance keeps the sounds of the user's own for the rest timer (`sounds`, v1.4.5). Absent on an instance from before; the app then keeps them on the device.

avatar.description: This instance keeps the user's profile picture (`avatar.m`, a 256 px square, v1.4.5). It is served like every other file, from the caller's own folder only. Absent on an instance from before; the app then keeps the picture on the device that set it.

workouts.description: This instance keeps the files a logged workout's `media` list names too, not only a custom exercise's. Absent on an instance from before; the app then offers photos and videos on custom exercises only.

days.description: This instance also keeps the files of progress photos filed under a day (`dayPhotos`, a photo for a day without a workout). Absent on an instance from before; the app then only adds photos to logged workouts there.

sets.description: This instance also keeps the files of a form video filmed for one set (`workouts[].entries[].sets[].media`, v1.4.4). Absent on an instance from before; the app then keeps a set's video on the phone that filmed it and never uploads it.

MediaConfig.description: The instance's media caps (`MEDIA_*`), in MB of 2^20 bytes. Absent when the instance runs with `MEDIA_UPLOADS=0`.

mime.description: What the bytes are, not necessarily what was declared.

existed.description: The server already had this file.

bytes.description: What the profile's stored files take.

confidential.description: Whether a client secret is set (never the secret).

logout.description: OIDC_LOGOUT is on and the provider has an end_session_endpoint.

OwnerProof.description: Either a passkey assertion made for this request (`cid` + `credential`), or the profile's current password (`current`), which counts only while `PASSWORD_LOGIN` is on. Each assertion is good for one request: its challenge is spent by it.

WebAuthnAuthenticationCredential.description: AuthenticationResponseJSON: the value `startAuthentication()` resolves with, sent back verbatim.

lastUsed.description: ISO timestamp of the last sign-in or confirmation with it.

password.description: The profile has a password and `PASSWORD_LOGIN` is on, so `current` can prove an addition or a removal.

lastWayIn.description: Removing any one passkey would be refused (409 `last-way-in`).

deleteBlocked.description: Present when deleting this profile (`POST /api/account/delete`) would be refused before any proof is checked: `last-admin`, the only admin while other profiles remain. The delete sheet says so before asking for a passkey or the password; the delete itself still checks.

PushSubscription.description: The browser's PushSubscription.toJSON(); only these fields are stored.

owner.description: Present (true) only for the instance owner.

oidc.description: Present (true) when the profile is linked to the configured identity provider.

SessionUser.description: The caller's identity, as returned by /api/me and the sign-in routes.

summary.description: A plan's routines and exercise ids

by.description: The uploader, read fresh on every answer. Always there.

consentId.description: The consent text the uploader agreed to when sharing it.

mod.description: The last moderation step: on your own hidden, removed or pending items (action and when), and in the admin list (also who and why).

importers.description: Admin list only: how many people imported it.

consent.description: Admin list only: the consent version agreed to, and when.

SharedItem.description: One item of the community library, as a client sees it (docs/dev/SHARED-LIBRARY-API.md).

_ts.description: Client-set last-write timestamp (ms since epoch); drives sync.

_rev.description: Server-set revision, incremented on every accepted PUT. Ignored when sent by a client.

_wid.description: Server-set id of this write (16 hex characters), new on every accepted PUT.

_wids.description: The write ids of the documents this one descends from, oldest first (up to 50).

deleted.description: When entries were removed, per list and entry key ({ workouts: { <id>: ms } }, weigh-ins by day, favourites by exercise id). A negative stamp is an add-back after a removal. Never shrinks on the server; stamped for writers that do not stamp (see PUT /api/data).

edited.description: When each setting and plan day was last changed, ms ({ queue: ms, 'week.3': ms, … }). Never shrinks on the server; stamped for writers that do not stamp (see PUT /api/data).

lang.description: UI language code ("en", "de", "pt", …); also localizes pushes.

queue.description: A planner's floating week {ids, since, startsOn, label}. The week's sessions as an ordered queue, the first undone one is today's. Written by an API client or by the app's own rotation feature, read by the reminder tick.

week.description: Weekly plan: weekday (0=Sunday … 6) → routine id, or several (a list).

dayPlan.description: Per-date overrides: ISO date → routine id, or "rest". Wins over `week`.

exWeights.description: Per-exercise last/best weight memory: exercise id → {w, d}.

tz.description: IANA zone ("Europe/Zurich"); the user's own clock.

get.summary: Instance configuration
get.description:
The flags the login screen needs before anyone is signed in. Both reflect
environment variables on the server (`INVITE_ONLY`, `ALLOW_GUEST`), and so does
`password_login`, which is there only when `PASSWORD_LOGIN=1`, and `default_lang`,
which is there only when `DEFAULT_LANG` is set.

`media` is there unless the instance runs with `MEDIA_UPLOADS=0`, for everybody: the
caps are not a secret, and its absence is how the app knows this server does not
store photos and videos at all.

A caller with a valid session also gets a `coach` key: the block when the
instance has the AI Coach switched on **and** a provider connected, and `null`
when it has not. A caller with no session gets no key at all. The block names
the provider this instance talks to, which is the same fact
`GET /api/coach/disclosure` will not hand out unauthenticated.

The key is always present for a session, `null` included, so a client that
caches this answer can tell "no Coach on this instance" from "you were not
signed in when you asked" and knows whether asking again would change it.

get.summary: Health check
get.description:
Always public. Also reports how many user accounts exist.

The check writes: it creates and removes one empty file under `DATA_DIR`,
because a server whose data directory is full or read-only has every write
path broken while the port still answers. It is a 503 when that fails — the
container healthcheck (`wget --spider`) reads the status and nothing else.

The probe runs at most once every five seconds and the answer in between is
the last one, so a poll can be that stale. The route is unauthenticated, and
one disk write per request is not something to leave open to anyone.

200.description: The server is up and its data directory is writable.

503.description: The data directory could not be written — a full disk, or a mount that came back read-only. Nothing that stores anything will work until it is fixed; the reason is in the container log.

post.summary: Delete your own account and everything of yours
post.description:
The signed-in account removes itself for good, with the same clean-up as
`/api/admin/user/delete`: the user record, their passkeys, their push
subscriptions, their live presence, their training history file, their
uploaded photos and videos (`DATA_DIR/uploads/<uid>/`) and any Coach credential
stored for them. Not reversible. The body carries the account's name, typed back
by its owner, and the same proof as setting a password (see OwnerProof): a
passkey assertion made for this request, or the current password while
`PASSWORD_LOGIN` is on. A paired phone (Bearer token) cannot hold a passkey for
the server, so for a profile with no password that counts the pairing itself is
the proof (audited as `device`; the app asks the phone's own screen lock first);
a profile with one sends the current password from the phone too. Cookie
sessions always need the proof. The name and the last-admin rule are checked
before the proof is asked. The last admin is refused while any other profile remains (the
instance would be left with nobody to run it); the only profile on an instance
may delete itself. Clears the caller's cookie; every other session and Bearer
token of the account stops working with it. Audited as `auth.account.delete`,
with the name and the proof it was made with (`passkey`, `password`, `device`); a refused proof as
`auth.proof.fail` with `act: account-delete`.

get.summary: Come back from the identity provider
get.description:
The redirect URI to register at the provider: `<ORIGIN>/api/oidc/callback` (or
OIDC_REDIRECT_URI). Checks the `state` and the flow cookie, trades the code at the
token endpoint with the PKCE verifier, and verifies the ID token: the signature against
the provider's JWKS (RS*, PS*, ES*, EdDSA; never `none` or HS*), `iss`, `aud`/`azp`,
`exp`, `iat`, `nbf` and the `nonce`. Groups and the e-mail are read from userinfo when
the ID token has none.

Then: a profile linked to this identity signs in; otherwise, with OIDC_EMAIL_LINKING=1,
a profile whose sign-in e-mail matches a `email_verified: true` address is linked;
otherwise a new profile is made, if the groups let this person in (OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS,
or an `access=` rule in OIDC_ROLE_MAP) and FIRST_USER_ADMIN applies as for any sign-up.
Answers 302 to the app with `?oidc=signed-in|linked|confirmed` and a session cookie, or
`?oidc-error=<code>`: `state`, `token`, `provider`, `cancelled`, `group`, `link-needed`,
`invite`, `disabled`, `taken`, `already-linked`, `wrong-account`, `link-expired`,
`throttled`. In app mode, 302 to `opengym://oidc?code=…&astate=…` (or `error=`) and no
cookie. Rate-limited per address; wrong states and tokens count toward the address pause.

get.summary: Leave for the identity provider
get.description:
A browser navigation, not a fetch. Answers 302 to the provider's authorization
endpoint with the authorization code flow, PKCE (S256), a fresh `state` and `nonce`,
and sets a 10-minute `gymoidc` cookie (`__Host-gymoidc` over https) that ties the
callback to this browser. `mode`: `web` (default), `app` (the phone app, see below),
`link` (Settings, with the `ticket` from POST /api/oidc/link, in the browser signed in
as that profile), or `reauth` (sign in at the provider again, `prompt=login`, so the
next change to a way in may use `provider: true` as its proof).

For `mode=app`, `return` must be exactly `opengym://oidc`, `challenge` the base64url
SHA-256 of a verifier only the app holds (43 characters), and `astate` the app's own
state, which comes back unchanged. Anything else is a 400, never a redirect.

get.description: Returns the caller's entire app state as one JSON blob, or `{"state": null}` if nothing has been synced yet, together with `rev`, the server's revision of that document (0 when there is none). A client keeps the `rev` it last read or wrote and sends it back as `baseRev` on the next push, which lets the server refuse a write over a document the client never saw (see the 409 on PUT).

put.description:
Replaces the stored state wholesale (atomic write; there is no merge on the
server). The `active` field (an in-progress workout) is stripped before
saving: a running session belongs to the device running it. Body limit 5 MiB.

With `baseRev` the write is conditional: it goes through only when `baseRev`
equals the document's current revision, and answers 409 with the current
document otherwise; the client merges the two and pushes again with the
revision it was given. Without `baseRev` the write is unconditional (clients
from before revisions, and deliberate replaces such as a backup import). The
server stamps the new revision into the document as `_rev`; a `_rev` sent by
the client is ignored.

The records of removals (`deleted`) and of edits (`edited`) never shrink: the
stored ones are joined into the write (a reset keeps its own). A writer that does
not stamp its own changes (no `stamped: true`; an API script, an older app) and
sends the current `baseRev` gets them stamped by the server, at the server's time:
every entry it removed (a workout, routine, custom exercise, weigh-in, card,
profile or favourite), every setting and plan day it changed (`queue`,
`week.<day>`, …), and every entry it edited (`_ts`, per field `_f`). That keeps a
planner's new week, or a routine it removed, from being undone by a phone that
reconnects later with an older change. A setting, plan day or entry field whose
stored stamp (`edited`, `_f`) is later than the one the writer sends back keeps the
stored value: the writer never saw that change, so send back the `edited` and `_f`
you read. A writer that sends no `edited` at all is not held to it. An entry the document holds while a
removal on record says it was deleted after its last edit is kept and marked as
added back.

Such a writer also cannot delete what it does not know: a field of the stored
document, of a stored routine, workout, custom exercise, card or profile, of a
routine's exercise, or of a logged exercise or set that its copy leaves out comes
back from the stored copy (an older app rebuilds an exercise from the fields it
knows, which dropped pyramid sets made on an updated device). Only the fields
v1.3.9 itself removes (a superset link, a note, a cleared set value, …) can be
removed this way. Send `stamped: true` to remove anything else.

Every accepted write also starts the grace period of each stored file (tag `media`)
the new state no longer references, and stops it for each one it references again.
That bookkeeping never changes the answer.

put.summary: Upload one photo, GIF or video
put.description:
The body is the raw file; `Content-Type` must be one of the eight types below and
`Content-Length` is optional (chunked uploads are capped while they stream). The path
names the SHA-256 of the bytes, and the file is stored only if they hash to it.
Idempotent: uploading a file the server already has answers 200 with `existed: true`.

Optional header `X-OpenGym-Account`: the account id the upload is meant for. When it is
not the session's account (the browser signed in as someone else meanwhile) the upload
is refused with 409 `account-mismatch` and nothing is stored.

What is stored is decided by the file's first bytes, not by the declared type. The
declared type only has to be in the same category, a still (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF) or a
video (MP4, MOV, WebM), or a sound (a 16-bit PCM WAV, `audio/wav`): a JPEG declared as a GIF is stored as the JPEG it is, a video
declared as an image is refused. The cap of the kind the bytes turned out to be applies
(`MEDIA_IMAGE_MAX_MB`, `MEDIA_GIF_MAX_MB`, `MEDIA_VIDEO_MAX_MB`, `MEDIA_AUDIO_MAX_MB`), and an MP4 or MOV must
be a well-formed file no longer than `MEDIA_VIDEO_MAX_SEC` (+1 s), read from its
headers. HEIC/AVIF, SVG, HTML and every other type are refused; the app converts HEIC
photos before uploading. The server never decodes or alters a file: the app has already
re-encoded photos and removed video metadata on the device.

Checked in this order: session (401), the hourly budget and at most two uploads at once
per profile (429), the declared type (415), a declared length over the cap (413 before
a byte is read), already stored (200), the quota (413 `media-quota`; files the profile
already dropped get one hour instead of the grace to make room), free disk (507), then
while and after streaming: size (413), hash (400), sniffed type (415), sniffed cap
(413), video checks (415/413). No bytes for 60 s ends the upload with 408. A refused
upload is read and discarded up to twice its cap, so the answer reaches the client.

A new file that the profile's state does not reference yet starts its grace period
at once, so a state push that never comes does not keep it forever.
